text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH GPU_QUEUE_LENGTH for pool `gpu-main` (avg queue 4800, p99 enqueue latency 3.2s) — triggering page to #incidents and on-call.

oncall-ellis: seeing this, thanks. I'm paged in, joining. Can someone post the top-level graphs (queue length, active GPUs, autoscale events)?

ops-raj: linking dashboards — https://dash.redwood.io/d/gpu-pool/gpu-main?from=now-30m&to=now — queue spiked ~15m ago, pods didn't scale after 3 autoscale attempts. max_pools cap hit at 48/48.

ml-runtime-lu: digging into serving logs. We're seeing a ton of prefix-cache misses (x1000/min) after last config push at 03:12 UTC. Config diff: `prefix_cache.ttl_seconds` changed from `3600` -> `60`. Also continuous_batching.max_delay bumped down to `10ms` in the same roll — that increases batch churn.

support-amy: customer reports: "requests stalled, streaming stalls and then 429s" — 7 accounts flagged so far, support ticket IDs linked in thread.

samir: autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts but pods stuck in Creating->Failed because kubequota blocked new pods due to a transient nodepool update. We hit two limits in parallel: pool max (48) and cluster new-pod throttle (5/min).

ops-raj: immediate mitigation plan: 1) increase pool max to 80 temporarily 2) bump cluster new pod throttle 3) revert prefix cache TTL to 3600 4) toggle continuous batching back to previous parameters. I'll run steps 1+2 now.

ops-raj: running command: ```
rbctl pools update gpu-main --max 80
rbctl cluster update --name prod --max-new-pods-per-minute 50
```

infra-bot: cluster update queued, node autoscaler will allow higher pod creation rate.

oncall-ellis: doing a quick canary rollback of the runtime config to the previous config hash `cfg@2026-03-15T03:10Z`. Maya can you prepare the rollback?

maya: rolling back now: `runtimectl apply --env prod --file /configs/runtime/cfg-2026-03-15.json --force` — patch applied, restarting a subset of routers. Watching metrics.

ml-runtime-lu: after rollback we should see prefix-cache miss rate drop and hit ratio recover; also continuous batches will re-aggregate fewer tiny batches which lowers per-token overhead.

ops-raj: pool max increased, new pods creating — creating 20 new pods. queue length dropped from 4.8k -> 1.2k within 6m. p50 enqueue latency from 1.1s -> 240ms.

support-amy: customers reporting improvement, one account still impacted intermittently (ticket #4371). Marking as partial customer impact.

samir: note: the autoscaler attempted to scale earlier but was rate-limited by `orchestrator.max_new_pods_per_minute=5` — config change to that throttle was intentional for stability during maintenance but not aligned with pool max changes. We'll need to reconcile.

oncall-ellis: handoff: I'm staying on for next 45m, but need to hand to ops-raj at 04:30 UTC. Raj, you'll take ownership for mitigation completion and postmortem.

ops-raj: ack. Current status: queue 600, active GPUs 66/80, prefix-cache miss rate trending down x20 -> now at 30/min (baseline ~2/min), continuous_batching metrics back to baseline.

ml-runtime-lu: root cause hypothesis: two simultaneous config changes in a single deploy: (A) prefix_cache.ttl_seconds shortened to 60s causing cache churn and more upstream work per request, (B) continuous_batching.max_delay reduced which increased small-batch frequency. Combined they increased per-request latency and GPU acceptance churn, causing queue buildup and pushing autoscaler to the pool cap. The cluster-level new-pod throttle prevented further scale which left queue to grow and user-facing 429s.

oncall-ellis: mitigation complete enough to restore service. Current customer impact: "degraded" for a short window, now "partial". I'll open the incident ticket and assign Sev2.

ops-raj: immediate postmortem action items: - revert risky combined changes into separate canaries - add pre-deploy check for prefix_cache.ttl diffs >10% - update autoscaler to ignore maintenance throttles for critical pools - add alert that correlates queue growth with pool max being reached - run a loadtest that simulates prefix-cache misses to validate scaling behaviour.

support-amy: I'll follow up with affected customers and post status updates in their tickets once Raj posts the incident timeline.

maya: creating roll-forward PR to lock prefix_cache.ttl_seconds to >=300s for major pools and add gating test. PR: https://git.redwood/infer/runtime-configs/pulls/512

infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0315-09, pager duty: assigned to ops-raj, severity: 2.

oncall-ellis: handing to ops-raj now. If anything regresses ping me directly.

ops-raj: taking over. Will draft timeline and run through rollback verification and autoscaler config changes. ETA 60m for postmortem draft.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident marked as mitigated (partial customer impact). Next steps: postmortem, config gating, and an automated regression test for batching+cache interactions.

samir: saving logs and attaching full debug dump to incident ticket. Reminder: don't delete the rollback config until postmortem is complete.

maya: noted. Adding unit/regression tests to PR.

support-amy: will update customers and close tickets when postmortem is published.

ops-raj: final note: big lesson — subtle parameter combos (cache TTL + batching window) can have multiplicative impact. We'll treat those as a paired-change risk in deployment playbooks.
